name_reason: Already fully compliant: data_fd2_ prefix (game global), chapter domain, ch20 is a meaningful chapter ID (chapters 1..30, kept), end_scene1 names the end-handler scene-1 phase, char_pos_x_table reflects both the table data type and the X-position semantics. No Ghidra address residue (no hex suffix equal to its own/another address; 0x521F6 does not appear in the name).
purpose: Const lookup table of scene-1 character X tile positions for the Chapter 20 end-scene; one byte per runtime-char slot 0..15.
logic_summary: fd2_chapter_20_end (its only reader) MOVSDx4-copies the 16 bytes from 0x521F6 into stack scratch (scene1_x[16]), then in the slot 0..15 placement loop writes scene1_x[i] into runtime_char[i].bPos_x (paired with the scene1 Y table at 0x52206 for bPos_y) and sets sprite_state[1]=1. The symbol is one of the four chapter-20 2-phase ending tables: scene1 X @ 0x521F6, scene1 Y @ 0x52206, scene2 X @ 0x52216 (9B), scene2 Y @ 0x5221F (9B).
element_semantics: Element i = world X tile coordinate for runtime char slot i (i=0..15) when placing the party for the Chapter 20 end-scene 1. Values 0x21..0x24 (33..36) are battlefield tile X coordinates.
notes: Src comment block (chend2.c lines 34-42) already documents all four tables accurately/concisely in ASCII; verified against disasm (0x23e8b MOV ESI,0x521f6; MOVSD.REP with ECX=4 = 16 bytes) and decomp, so comment kept unchanged. Ghidra plate content previously lived in the deprecated PRE_COMMENT field; migrated to PLATE_COMMENT via run_script_inline Java API (set PLATE_COMMENT, cleared PRE_COMMENT) per project_ghidra_data_plate_mechanism, refined to match the src conclusion. Const confirmed: only 2 xrefs, both READ/DATA from fd2_chapter_20_end, zero writers. No src .c edit was needed (comment kept), so only the shard is staged.
